cited.quote: the Government fix the State Advised Price for sugarcane for 2016-17 Sugar season at Rs.2,850/- per M.T.
the Government have fixed State Advised Price for 2015-16 as Rs.2,850/- per M.T.

rationale: C2 (GO of 2017-01-05) fixes the 2016-17 State Advised Price at Rs.2,850, the same figure as the 2015-16 price it recalls, so no increase is shown. C1 and C3 move to revenue sharing with a transitional incentive that holds the earlier price. Only related steps, none a higher SAP.

cited.quote: So far 52,628 Anganwadi centres have been provided with LPG connection.
Supply of Drinking water to Anganwadies and also modernizing the Anganwadi Kitchen Sheds with Gas connection,

rationale: C2 reports LPG connection with stove and pressure cooker for 52,628 of 54,439 centres, so not all; C4 and C1 show the modernisation continuing in phases. C3 is the earliest GO in the extracts (2017-11-15) allowing MLACDS funds for gas connections in Anganwadi kitchens. Coverage is near-complete but not universal.

cited.quote: from Rs. 25.00 lakhs to Rs. 40.00 lakhs for State Government Employees
The maximum advance admissible to a State Government Servant under this category is Rs.25 lakh

rationale: C1 is G.O.(Ms) No.24 of 2021-02-02 enhancing the House Building Advance ceiling for State Government employees from Rs.25 lakh to Rs.40 lakh, effective from the date of issue. C2 shows the ceiling was Rs.25 lakh before. Matches the promised amount.

cited.quote: Government has been taking steps to bring the granite bearing Government lands for auction

rationale: The extracts concern granite quarries (C1 audit, C2 and C5 a lease lapse, C3 and C4 policy notes) but none shows a new granite policy, GO or draft. C4 only says steps are being taken to auction granite lands, which is not a policy formulation.

cited.quote: from 24.05.2016 onwards, the working hours of TASMAC retail vending liquor shops
from 12 noon to 10 pm as against the earlier working hours of 10 am to 10 pm

rationale: C1 states the government ordered reduced working hours and that from 24.05.2016 TASMAC shops open 12 noon to 10 pm instead of 10 am to 10 pm; C2 repeats this. The change took effect the day after the government took office, so it counts for this government.

cited.quote: RIDF XXII 2016-2017 - According administrative sanction for Rs.25192.19 lakh
Financial Sanction for a sum of Rs.12,00,00,000/- (Rupees Twelve Crore only)

rationale: C3 is G.O.(Ms) No.47 of 2017-03-14 sanctioning Rs.25192.19 lakh for school infrastructure in 149 government high schools; C5 (2019-01-30) is a further financial sanction of Rs.12 crore for infrastructure in tribal schools. Both are funds sanctioned for school infrastructure after the government took office.

cited.quote: for the construction of 149 school buildings in Rural areas for High schools upgraded during 2011-12
libraries, toilets, drinking water 129 facilities and compound walls are being provided by the Government

rationale: C4 (GO of 2017-03-14) gives administrative sanction for building 149 school buildings, an official step, but no extract shows that construction under it started. C2 only says facilities are being provided generally, with figures pooled from earlier years. Sanction given, start of work not shown.

cited.quote: 56 tanks pertaining to Vellore (28), Ramanathapuram (9) and Sivagangai (19) Districts at a cost of
104 tanks pertaining to Ramanathapuram, Vellore and Sivagangai Districts were completed

rationale: C1 (2017-07-09) reports PMKSY repair and restoration of tanks in Vellore, Ramanathapuram and Sivagangai taken up at Rs.27.30 crore; C2 reports 104 tanks in those three districts completed. C4 and C5 add Kudimaramath restoration GOs for them in 2019. Treating tanks as the lakes of the promise; the date is the earliest document reporting the works under way.

cited.quote: Concession Rules, 1959 have been amended suitably on 27.04.2017
to take the clay, silt, savudu and gravel from the beds of tanks, channels and reservoirs at free of cost

rationale: C2 reports the Tamil Nadu Minor Minerals Concession Rules were amended on 27.04.2017 so that potters, farmers and others may take clay and silt from water-body beds free of cost; C1 describes the same concession and its quantity limits and the scheme launch. This is a concession to take clay from government water bodies.

cited.quote: enhanced the free supply of electricity to handloom weavers from 100 units to 200 units bi-monthly
Scheme for Free Supply of Electricity to Handloom Weavers households @ 200 units

rationale: C1 states the free electricity for handloom weavers was raised from 100 to 200 units bi-monthly with effect from 23.05.2016 (the day the government took office, so not before); C3 confirms the earlier 100-unit level and C5 lists the 200-unit scheme in the 2019 textile policy.

cited.quote: 500 TASMAC retail vending liquor shops have been closed with effect from 19.06.2016
of the 1000 Retail Vending shops which were closed on 19.06.2016 and 24.02.2017

rationale: C3 says the government ordered a reduction in the number of TASMAC shops and 500 were closed from 19.06.2016; C1 confirms 1000 shops closed on 19.06.2016 and 24.02.2017, and C2 notes further closures after court orders. Shops were reduced as promised.

cited.quote: A Comprehensive Input Supply and Management System ensuring quality of critical inputs besides improving the delivery mechanism

rationale: C1, C2 and C3 discuss horticulture schemes and input supply in general, and C3 lists an input supply system as a strategy. None shows a GO or dedicated step on timely quality inputs for horticulture and hill crops; C4 and C5 concern extension and review committees.

cited.quote: Expansion of Madurai Dairy is being carried
It has been proposed to increase the chilling capacity from 15.19 LLPD to 19.12 LLPD
It has also been proposed to establish a new automated dairy to handle 10.00 LLPD

rationale: C1 reports cold rooms, milk coolers and a Madurai dairy expansion under way; C3 reports 341 coolers installed and 218 more proposed; C4 only proposes a new Madhavaram dairy. No dated GO or sanction for a large new dairy or chillers appears, so only works in progress are shown.

cited.quote: New initiative of Financial Assistance to repair and renovation of Christian Churches
A scheme of providing financial assistance for repair and renovation of Christian churches has been introduced

rationale: C2 is G.O.(Ms) No.71 dated 20.12.2016 sanctioning Rs.1 crore as a grant for repair and renovation of Christian churches and framing guidelines. C1 and C5 show the scheme introduced in 2016-17 with Rs.44.62 lakh sanctioned for 18 churches.

cited.quote: accord administrative sanction for the construction of various infrastructure for supply chain management of Fruits, Vegetables and other Perishables
111 Numbers of cold storage facilities with the capacity to handle 13,565 MTs have been created

rationale: C4 is G.O.Ms.No.169 of 2016-06-21 sanctioning Rs.398.75 crore for supply chain infrastructure for fruits and vegetables in 10 districts; C3 describes the primary processing centres with cold storage, and C1 reports cold storage facilities created across the State. Scope is broadly as promised, though the main project covers 10 districts.

cited.quote: Implementation of Micro Irrigation Scheme under Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana during 2016-17
Small & Marginal farmers are eligible to avail 100% subsidy and other category farmers can avail 75% subsidy.
Tamil Nadu is the only State extending 100% subsidy to Small and Marginal Farmers and 75% subsidy to Other Farmers.

rationale: C5 (G.O.Ms.No.290, 2016-09-23) releases the first instalment for the 2016-17 micro irrigation scheme; C4 (2017-02-07) states 100% subsidy for small and marginal farmers and 75% for others; C1 and C2 confirm the State continued these rates.

cited.quote: the Tamil Nadu Lokayukta Act, 2018 was enacted and brought into force with effect from 13.11.2018
Tamil Nadu Lokayukta Act, 2018 was enacted and with the appointment of the Chairman and four Members

rationale: C3 states the Tamil Nadu Lokayukta Act, 2018 was enacted and brought into force from 13.11.2018, and C2 shows a Search Committee constituted under it; C4 reports the Lokayukta functional. The state Lokayukta law was brought in.

cited.quote: Ploughing subsidy @ Rs.1250 / ha would be extended as back ended subsidy to the Farmers
One Time Assistance of 25% of the project cost, with a ceiling of Rs.10 crore

rationale: The promise does not say which clusters. C2 and C5 describe dryland clusters with 50% and 80% subsidies, not 25%. C4 offers 25% assistance only for a trade facilitation centre. No extract shows clusters established with a 25 percent State subsidy.

No extract is about completing projects estimated at 790 crore rupees by 2018. C5's 790 refers to buildings for access audit, and the others cover unrelated works and schemes, so nothing can be judged.

None of the extracts mentions Illandhorum Inaiyam or any internet or e-service of that name. They cover horticulture schemes, real estate rules and an IFHRMS computer purchase. No extract is about the commitment.
